title: Nested source-operation deadline floors can overrun the metadata client's allowance
outcome: A source observation retains one admitted absolute window through nested owner helpers; queue/lock waits do not silently re-floor it beyond the metadata client's funded wait.
acceptance: The source-owner metadata and observation entry/caller inventory identifies each admission point and passes its admitted absolute deadline through nested helpers without repeatedly adding a new minimum window; longer caller windows remain supported and zero/expired admission remains refused.

A deterministic scripted-clock or controlled-admission behavioral check covers blocking-queue/authority delay and proves the metadata client can receive the definitive host result within its funded envelope; no real minute waits and no timeout-formula pins are added.

No effective limit on an already issued operation becomes shorter without Greg's recorded word; any required change to the existing longer metadata window is coordinated with the separate funded-metadata-window work.
